name: research
note: The grounded-research write step — GROUNDED_WRITE_INSTRUCTION over a canned numbered source pack. Quality is now VERIFIED, not counted: each '> quote' must be a VERBATIM substring of the source its claim cited. `sources` mirrors the [n] bodies in `user` so run.py can string-match — a model that emits quote-shaped lines it did not copy scores 0 verbatim (the counting harness couldn't tell the difference).
system: You write a study note using ONLY the numbered sources provided. Output a list of claims, one per item. For each claim: write ONE sentence on its own line, starting with '- ' and ending with the citation '[n]' of the source it comes from; then on the NEXT line, starting with '> ', copy a SHORT VERBATIM quote from that same source that supports the claim — copy the words EXACTLY, do not paraphrase and do not shorten across gaps. Cite every claim. Use only the numbered sources, never your own knowledge, and never state anything the sources do not. If the sources do not answer the question, reply with a single '- ' line saying so and no citation. Output only the list — no preamble, no headings, no Sources section.
user:
Question: What is retrieval-augmented generation and why is it used?

[1] Retrieval-augmented generation — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RAG
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a technique that grants generative artificial intelligence models information retrieval capabilities. It modifies interactions so that the model responds to user queries with reference to a specified set of documents, using this information to supplement its pre-existing training data.

[2] Reducing hallucination — https://example.org/rag-hallucination
Because the model grounds its answer in retrieved passages rather than only its parameters, RAG reduces the tendency to fabricate facts, and lets a system cite the source of each claim so a reader can verify it.

[3] Keeping knowledge current — https://example.org/rag-fresh
RAG allows a model to use data that was not part of its training set, so the knowledge can be updated by changing the document store rather than retraining the model.
